title: First recognised Neanderthal fossil found
place: Kleine Feldhofer Grotte, Neander Valley, Germany
summary: In 1856 schoolteacher Johann Carl Fuhlrott recognised bones from Kleine Feldhofer Grotte in the Neander Valley as distinct from modern humans. Neanderthal 1 became the first recognised Neanderthal fossil.
why: The first fossil recognised as another kind of human, though experts disputed it for decades.

notes.problem: 'Quarry workers found' is not in the source; 'first proof' overclaims: Engis 2 (1829) and Gibraltar 1 (1848) were found earlier, and Virchow's opposition stalled acceptance until about 1900.
